house_heating_fuel.unit: percent of occupied housing units reporting heating fuel (occupied units for 1980+)
notes: 1940: utility gas and bottled gas were combined (shown under utility_gas_pct); electricity was collected but not tabulated.
1950: electricity was tallied only for noncentral heating systems.

units_in_structure.unit: percent of housing units (US counts included)
notes: 1940/1950: "other" = trailers, tourist cabins, boats; 1960-2000 have a Mobile home column; 1990/2000 add Other; 1980 adds boat/tent/van.
1950 attached includes row houses and semi-detached (2 side-by-side).
1970/1980 counts restricted to year-round units. Some count tokens in source files are truncated and returned as null.

crowding.unit: crowded = more than 1.00 persons per room (1.01 or more); severely = 1.51 or more; percent of occupied units reporting persons per room
notes: 1950: states do not quite add to the US total (Census note).

sewage_disposal.unit: 1940-1960: units lacking a flush toilet; 1970-1990: sewage disposal method

notes: 1990 all housing units; 1970 and 1980 year-round units only. 1970 drilled/dug split not available.

plumbing.unit: housing units with / lacking complete plumbing facilities; lacking_pct = percent of units reporting
notes: Complete plumbing = hot and cold piped water, bathtub or shower, flush toilet. Earlier censuses required exclusive use by the unit occupants; dropped in 1990 (Census page).

median_home_value.unit: dollars, median value of owner-occupied (specified) units as published; unadjusted and adjusted to 2000 dollars

source_urls.index: https://www.census.gov/data/tables/time-series/dec/coh-plumbing.html (also coh-fuels, coh-units, coh-sewage, coh-water, coh-crowding, coh-values, coh-owner)

notes: State rows keep percentages only (US rows keep counts); counts for states are in the source text files.
Census page: complete plumbing facilities = hot and cold piped water, a bathtub or shower, and a flush toilet; earlier censuses required exclusive use, dropped in 1990.
Census page: in 1990 only 1 percent of homes lacked complete plumbing; in 1940 nearly half did.
Some count tokens truncated in the source files (e.g. 1940 other units, 2000 5+ units) are null; percentages are intact.
